facts.statement: Archaeornithura lived during the Hauterivian age approximately 130.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: The specimens have been dated to the Hauterivian age, 130.7 million years ago

facts.statement: Archaeornithura meemannae is the oldest known member of the ornithuromorph lineage, which includes all modern birds and their extinct relatives.
facts.quote: making A. meemannae the oldest known ornithuromorph, the lineage that gave rise to modern birds

facts.statement: Two fossil specimens of Archaeornithura were found in the Huajiying Formation in Hebei Province, China.
facts.quote: Both specimens of A. meemannae, the holotype STM7-145 and the paratype STM7-163, were discovered in the interbedded shale rocks of the Huajiying Formation in Hebei Province, China

facts.statement: The species was named and described by an international team led by Wang and Zhou Zhonge from the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing.
facts.quote: They were named and described by an international team of paleontologists led by Wang and Zhou Zhonge of the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology, Beijing

facts.statement: The discovery of Archaeornithura was announced in the journal Nature Communications in May 2015.
facts.quote: The discovery was announced in Nature Communications in May 2015

facts.statement: Some feathers of Archaeornithura feature a central groove, a trait associated with derived flight feathers.
facts.quote: Some Archaeornithura feathers feature a central groove, a trait thought to arise from derived flight feathers

facts.statement: Archaeornithura appears to have been adept at flying.
facts.quote: The species appears to have been adept at flying

facts.statement: Archaeornithura is classified within the family Hongshanornithidae.
facts.quote: Archaeornithura was placed in the Hongshanornithidae

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis identified Archaeornithura as the sister taxon of Tianyuornis.
facts.quote: Archaeornithura was shown to be the sister taxon of Tianyuornis

facts.statement: The time range for Archaeornithura is estimated from 132.6 to 125.77 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hauterivian to Hauterivian (132.6 to 125.77 million years ago)

facts.statement: Archaeornithura is the first ornithuromorph fossil discovered in the Huajiying Formation.
facts.quote: Archaeornithura is the first ornithuromorph found in the Huajiying Formation

facts.statement: The thighbone of Archaeornithura is short relative to the length of the tarsometatarsus.
facts.quote: The thighbone is short relative to the tarsometatarsus

facts.statement: Researchers Zhou and Wang hypothesize that these avian traits may have helped ornithuromorphs survive the Cretaceous-Paleogene mass extinction.
facts.quote: Zhou y Wang conjeturan que estos rasgos avianos pudieron haber ayudado a los ornituromorfos a sobrevivir a la extinción masiva del Cretácico-Terciario
